description: Reconcile the existing client-side auto-sync in inbox.tsx with the new server-side sync so the two never fight or create duplicates, fix the dedup inconsistency, and stop silently dropping unmatched owner tags. The server sync (FEAT-002) is now the reliable guarantee; the client effect becomes a fast, best-effort front-of-queue helper that is (a) no longer admin-only for visibility of what is happening and (b) uses the SAME dedup key as lead creation. Manual claim / markMine / assign mutations MUST remain behaviorally unchanged.
steps: Read the current auto-sync useEffect + syncTagged mutation in src/routes/_authenticated/inbox.tsx (around the `syncedRef` / `syncTagged` block) to confirm exact current behavior before editing.

Fix the dedup inconsistency in the auto-sync useEffect pre-check: it currently skips based on parseFrom(e.from).address (the RELAY/sender address) while syncTagged creates/dedups on resolveLeadFields' [realEmail, senderAddr]. Change the pre-check so it does NOT prematurely skip on the sender address alone. Let syncTagged's resolveLeadFields + existingLeadFor([realEmail, senderAddr]) be the single source of truth for whether a lead already exists. Keep the per-session syncedRef guard (so the same thread isn't reprocessed in one session) but only add a threadId to syncedRef AFTER it has been handed to syncTagged (or confirmed already-a-lead by the unified dedup), not before parsing.

Surface unmatched owner tags instead of dropping them: when claimedOwner(e.labels) is non-null but matchOwnerToUser returns null, collect these and show a non-blocking UI hint (e.g. a small toast or an inline note/badge count like 'N tagged emails could not be matched to a team member — check the label spelling') rather than silently continuing. Do not create a lead for unmatched tags (the server function logs them). Keep this cheap and non-spammy (e.g. one aggregated toast per load, guarded so it doesn't repeat every poll).

Because the server-side sync (FEAT-002) now guarantees coverage, relax or annotate the admin-only gate: the client effect may remain best-effort but should not be the ONLY path. Simplest safe change: keep the client auto-create effect but add a clear code comment that it is a best-effort accelerator and the authoritative sync is the gmail-tag-sync cron function; ensure that when a non-admin views the inbox, tagged-but-unmatched and tagged emails are at least surfaced (matching filters/badges) even if the client does not itself insert. If enabling client-side insert for the current user's OWN tagged emails is low-risk under RLS (a sales user can insert leads assigned to themselves), allow the client to auto-create leads for emails tagged to the CURRENT user only, deferring all other owners to the server sync. Choose the approach that avoids RLS insert failures for non-admins and avoids duplicates with the server run.
Verify the manual mutations claim, markMine, and assign are untouched (same resolveLeadFields, same existingLeadFor, same toasts, same Gmail relabel).
Add/adjust code comments so the relationship between the client effect and the gmail-tag-sync cron is documented in inbox.tsx.
acceptance_criteria: The auto-sync pre-check no longer skips a thread solely because the relay sender address exists; dedup is decided by the unified [realEmail, senderAddr] key via existingLeadFor.
A thread is only added to syncedRef after it is dispatched to syncTagged or confirmed already-a-lead by the unified dedup, so a genuinely-new tagged email is never skipped by a stale pre-check.
Tagged emails whose owner tag matches no team member are surfaced to the user (aggregated, non-spammy) and are never turned into an unassigned/duplicate lead by the client.

Non-admin users do not hit RLS insert failures: the client either only inserts leads assigned to the current user (allowed by RLS) or defers to the server sync; no toast errors for permission denials in normal use.
claim, markMine, and assign mutations are byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.
inbox.tsx documents that gmail-tag-sync (server cron) is the authoritative guarantee and the client effect is a best-effort accelerator.
verification: Read the git diff of inbox.tsx and confirm the syncedRef is populated only after dispatch/confirmation and the sender-address-only pre-skip is removed.
Confirm existingLeadFor is used for the dedup decision in the effect path (unified with syncTagged), not parseFrom(e.from).address alone.
Confirm unmatched tags produce a single aggregated, guarded hint (not one per email, not on every 60s poll).
Confirm claim/markMine/assign mutation bodies are unchanged by diffing against main.
Note in findings that build/typecheck cannot run in-sandbox (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY); CI must confirm the React/TS changes compile.
review_fixes_2026-09-03: Addressed review issues #5 (client half) and #6 in src/routes/_authenticated/inbox.tsx. Issue #6 (client self-scope leaves some roles unable to insert): the auto-sync insert was gated only on ownership (owner.id === user.id), but leads_insert RLS requires admin/sales/bd; a user whose only roles are documentation/accounts/renewals would hit a denial toast. Added canInsertLeads = isAdmin || hasRole('sales') || hasRole('bd') (pulled hasRole from useAuth) and gate the effect on `if (!canInsertLeads) continue;` BEFORE the existing race-avoidance self-scope check (`if (!isAdmin && owner.id !== user?.id) continue;`), which is preserved unchanged. Added canInsertLeads to the effect deps. Issue #5 (created_by attribution): syncTagged now sets created_by: r.owner.id (the matched owner) instead of user.id, so attribution is identical to the server cron (which sets created_by = profile.id) regardless of which path wins. This is RLS-safe because leads_insert has NO per-row created_by/assigned_to constraint (verified against setup/COMBINED_DATABASE_SETUP.sql). Manual claim/markMine/assign are UNCHANGED — they keep created_by: user.id (explicit human action) and their existing assigned_to semantics. Verified by inspection only (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY; no bun/tsc).
findings: Edited only src/routes/_authenticated/inbox.tsx. Changes: (1) Removed the premature sender-address-only pre-skip in the auto-sync useEffect. Previously it skipped a thread when parseFrom(e.from).address was already in leadByEmail (relay/sender addr only), which disagreed with syncTagged's [realEmail, senderAddr] dedup and caused genuinely-new tagged emails to be dropped. Now existingLeadFor([realEmail, senderAddr]) inside syncTagged is the single source of truth. (2) syncedRef timing fixed: a threadId is now added to syncedRef ONLY after it is handed to syncTagged (pending.push path). Unmatched-tag threads are intentionally NOT added to syncedRef so a later profile rename/label correction can be re-evaluated. (3) Unmatched owner tags are surfaced instead of dropped: when claimedOwner(e.labels) is non-null but matchOwnerToUser returns null, the tags are collected, counted (unmatchedCount state -> persistent amber inline note in the toolbar Card), and a single aggregated toast.warning is shown. The toast is guarded by unmatchedNotedRef (a sorted signature of the unique unmatched tags) so it fires at most once per distinct set and never on every 60s poll. No lead is ever created for unmatched tags (the server gmail-tag-sync function logs these to email_log). (4) Step-4 approach chosen: (b) allow client-side auto-create for the CURRENT user's OWN tagged emails, plus keep admin insert for ANY matched owner; all other owners defer to the authoritative server sync. Reasoning: leads_insert RLS lets any sales/bd/admin insert (no per-row assigned_to check), so self-scoping for non-admins avoids RLS denial toasts AND avoids racing the server sync for other people's tags. The admin gate (`!isAdmin`) was thus relaxed from a hard early-return to a per-email scope check. Documented with a code comment block stating gmail-tag-sync (cron) is authoritative and this effect is a best-effort accelerator. Also added a persistent inline amber badge so non-admins see unmatched counts even after dismissing the toast. Manual mutations claim/markMine/assign are byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed via git diff; they do not appear in the diff).
